name: Cape Malay Chicken Curry
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1 tbsp (6 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 5.25 lb (2381 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium and cook the sliced onion slowly for 10 to 12 minutes, until it is deeply soft and golden. Cape Malay curry starts with patient onions, not fast ones.

Add the garlic and grated ginger and cook one minute, then add the red pepper flakes, ground coriander, italian seasoning, ground cumin, ground turmeric, garam masala, ground cinnamon and black pepper. Stir them in the hot oil for about 45 seconds until the kitchen smells like the spice aisle.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, scrape the bottom, and cook 10 minutes until the sauce darkens and thickens.
Add the chicken thighs, cut into large chunks, and turn them until every piece is coated. Cover and simmer 30 to 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and reads 165F.
Stir in the brown sugar and lemon juice. This is the step that makes it Cape Malay instead of generic, so taste as you go and adjust until it tastes bright and slightly sweet at the same time.
While it finishes, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Fold the cooked rice through the curry so every serving gets sauce and grain in the same scoop.

name: Carbonada (Chilean Beef, Corn and Squash Soup)
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 4.5 oz (130 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the chopped onion, garlic, red bell pepper, and celery in the vegetable oil until soft, about 8 minutes.
Cut the beef into small cubes, season with salt and pepper, and brown it in the same pot in batches.
Add the paprika, cumin, and oregano and stir for a minute so the spices bloom in the fat.
Cover everything with water, bring it to a simmer, and cook 35 to 40 minutes until the beef starts to give.
Add the potatoes, sweet potatoes, and carrots and simmer 15 minutes more.
Stir in the rice and cook another 15 to 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the soup has gone properly thick.
Add the green beans, corn, and peas in the last 5 minutes, then taste and correct the salt.

name: Caribbean Curry Beef with Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Blend most of the cilantro, the green onions, the jalapeno, half the garlic, and some of the onion into a rough green seasoning. Rub it into the cubed chuck roast and let it sit at least 30 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot, add the curry powder and cumin, and stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes until it darkens and smells toasted. Do not walk away.
Add the remaining chopped onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Add the seasoned beef and stir until every piece is coated in curry, then let it sear and stick a little before you add liquid.
Stir in the chopped tomato and the ketchup, add enough water to nearly cover, and simmer covered 60 to 75 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the peeled and chunked potatoes and simmer uncovered another 25 to 30 minutes, until they are soft and starting to break down and thicken the gravy.
Taste for salt and pepper and finish with the last of the chopped cilantro.

name: Carne en su Jugo Bowls
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 1.75 lb (794 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and cook it in a large pot until crisp. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and leave the fat behind.
Slice the steak thin against the grain, season it with salt, cumin, and black pepper, and sear it in the bacon fat in batches until just browned.
Husk and rinse the tomatillos, then blend them with the jalapenos, most of the cilantro, and the garlic into a rough green salsa.
Pour the salsa into the pot, scraping up everything stuck to the bottom, and simmer 10 minutes until it darkens slightly.
Return the beef with enough water to make it brothy, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the meat is tender.
Drain and rinse the beans and stir them in, then cook 5 more minutes so they warm through and pick up the salsa.
Finish each bowl with the crisped bacon, chopped raw onion, and the remaining cilantro.

name: Carne Guisada (Tex-Mex Beef and Potato Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the sirloin into small cubes, pat them dry, and season with salt, black pepper, cumin, and oregano.
Brown the beef in the olive oil in batches over high heat until it takes on real color.
Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and diced jalapeno and cook until soft, scraping the pot bottom clean.
Sprinkle the flour over everything and stir for a minute so it toasts rather than tasting raw.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice and the beef broth, along with the splash of soy sauce from the pantry list.
Cover and simmer low for 75 to 90 minutes, until the beef is tender and the liquid has reduced into a gravy that clings.
Taste for salt and heat, then cook the rice separately.

name: Cheeseburger Rice Bowls
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 bag (180 g)
steps: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Stir in the beef broth, diced tomatoes, ketchup, dijon, and garlic.
Simmer until the sauce reduces and coats the beef.
Cook the rice separately, then stir it into the skillet or serve it underneath.
Melt the shredded cheddar over the top before portioning into containers.

name: Cheesy Beef and Shells Casserole
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 37.25 oz dry (1058 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 18.5 oz (527 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 9.25 oz (264 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the pasta shells in salted water until just shy of al dente, then drain.

In your largest pot, brown the ground beef with the diced onion over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains; ground beef should hit 160F. Drain excess fat, then add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the tomato sauce, beef broth, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Simmer 5 to 7 minutes so it thickens slightly.
Fold in the drained shells and about two-thirds of the cheddar, stirring until the cheese melts into the sauce.
Scatter the remaining cheddar and the mozzarella over the top, drop the heat to low, and cover 3 to 4 minutes until the top layer melts.
Let it rest 5 minutes off the heat; the sauce tightens up and clings to the shells.

name: Cheesy Ground Beef Tortellini
ingredients: Cheese Tortellini (Great Value): 41.5 oz dry (1173 g)
1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 18.75 oz (529 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 28 oz (791 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground beef in your largest pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks, until no pink remains; ground beef should reach 160F. Drain excess fat.
Season with the garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, and pepper, then stir in the marinara sauce and bring to a simmer.
Add the cream cheese in chunks and stir until it melts into a creamy rosa-style sauce, 3 to 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the cheese tortellini in salted water until they float and are just tender, then drain.
Fold the tortellini into the sauce gently so they do not tear.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top, cover, and heat on low 3 to 4 minutes until melted. Rest 5 minutes before portioning.

name: Cheesy Pork Chop and Hash Brown Casserole
ingredients: Frozen Hash Browns (Great Value): 25.25 cups (2117 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 14 oz (397 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Preheat the oven to 350F. Season the pork chops with salt and pepper and sear them in a hot skillet, about 2 minutes per side, just for color. Set aside; they finish in the oven.
In the same skillet, melt the butter and cook the diced onions and sliced mushrooms 6 to 8 minutes until browned and their liquid has cooked off.
In your biggest bowl, mix the thawed hash browns, sour cream, chicken broth, the mushroom-onion mixture, half the cheddar, salt, and pepper.
Spread the hash brown mixture into two greased 9x13 pans and lay the seared chops on top.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes, then uncover, scatter the remaining cheddar over everything, and bake 10 to 15 more minutes until bubbly and the pork reaches at least 145F.
Rest 10 minutes, then cube the chops and fold everything together in your weighed pot so every portion gets pork, potatoes, and cheese.

name: Cheesy Smoked Sausage and Rice Skillet
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package directions and set it aside. Slightly undercooked is better than mushy since it will get stirred and reheated.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins, dice the onion, chop the red bell pepper and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the sausage coins until the edges darken, then set them aside.
Melt the butter in the same pan and cook the onion and pepper until they soften, then add the garlic, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and black pepper.
Add the broccoli florets and cook until they turn bright green and just tender. Overcooked broccoli goes gray and mealy in the fridge.
Fold the cooked rice and the browned sausage back into the skillet and stir everything together over low heat.
Kill the heat, scatter the shredded cheddar over the top, and cover for a couple of minutes so it melts before you stir it through.

name: Cheesy Taco Spaghetti
ingredients: Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 3.5 cans (992 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 7 oz (198 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until just shy of al dente, then drain, saving a cup of pasta water.
Meanwhile, brown the ground beef in your largest pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains; ground beef should hit 160F. Drain excess fat.
Add the garlic and diced jalapenos and cook 2 to 3 minutes, then stir in the taco seasoning and tomato paste.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Fold in the spaghetti with a splash of the reserved pasta water, then stir in the Mexican cheese blend until it melts into the sauce.
Top with the mozzarella, cover on low heat 3 to 4 minutes until melted, then finish with the sliced olives and chopped cilantro.

name: Cheesy Turkey Sausage and Vegetable Rice Casserole
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 1 can (385 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 18.75 oz (529 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large oven-safe pot, stir in the rice, cover, and simmer on low for 18 minutes, then set it aside covered.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the sliced smoked turkey sausage until the cut edges char, then set it aside.
In the same skillet, cook the diced onion, red bell pepper, and zucchini for 8 minutes over medium-high, hot enough that the zucchini colors instead of weeping.
Add the garlic and the drained corn, cook two minutes more, then season with salt and black pepper and return the sausage to the pan.
Whisk the flour into the milk in a jar until smooth, pour it into the skillet, and cook 4 to 5 minutes until it thickens into a sauce.
Off the heat, melt in about two thirds of the shredded cheddar, then fold the whole skillet into the cooked rice until evenly combined.
Spread it level, scatter the rest of the cheddar over the top, and broil 3 to 5 minutes until blistered. Watch it the entire time, then finish with torn fresh basil.

name: Cheesy Zucchini Beef and Rice Skillet
ingredients: Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (196 g)
Vegetable Oil (Great Value): 2 tbsp canola oil (40 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (2 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Rinse the rice and cook it according to the package. Set it aside to steam while you build the skillet.
Heat a large skillet over medium high heat with a little olive oil. Add the lean ground beef and brown it, breaking it apart as it cooks until there is no more pink.
Stir in the diced yellow onion and green bell peppers with a pinch of salt. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until they start to soften.
Add the diced zucchini, the taco seasoning, and the canned diced tomatoes with their juice. Stir it all together so the seasoning coats everything.
Let it simmer 5 to 7 minutes until the zucchini is tender. If it looks dry or starts to stick, splash in a quarter cup of water.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fat free cheddar until it melts into the mix. Serve over the cooked rice, or fold the rice right into the skillet.

name: Chicken with 40 Cloves of Garlic
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.75 lb (2117 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel all the garlic. Smash each clove with the flat of a knife first and the skins come off easily. Keep the cloves whole.
Season the chicken thighs with salt, pepper, cumin, thyme, and dill and brown them in the olive oil in batches until deeply colored. Set them aside.

Turn the heat down to medium-low, add all the garlic to the pan, and cook it slowly for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until the cloves turn golden and soft. Burnt garlic will ruin the entire pot, so low and slow is the only setting here.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pan clean, then return the chicken with any juices.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes until the chicken is tender and the garlic cloves have collapsed into the sauce.
Uncover and simmer 10 more minutes to reduce, mashing a few cloves against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce naturally.
Cook the rice and taste for salt before you portion.

name: Old-Fashioned Chicken and Dumplings
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.5 lb (2012 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces and simmer them in the chicken broth with the onion, carrots, celery, bay leaves, salt, and pepper for about 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the broth tastes like something.
Pull the chicken out, shred it, and return it to the pot. Fish out the bay leaves.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little cold water and stir it into the simmering pot to thicken the broth slightly. Cold water first, always, or you get lumps you will never break up.

Make the dumpling dough by cutting the cold butter into the flour with baking powder and salt until it looks like coarse crumbs, then stirring in the milk just until it comes together. Overworking the dough makes tough dumplings, so stop mixing while it still looks shaggy.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the surface of the simmering pot, spacing them apart since they will swell.
Cover tightly and steam 15 minutes without lifting the lid. Every peek releases the steam that is actually cooking them.
Cook the rice separately and put a scoop in the bottom of each container to stretch the batch further.

name: Chicken Biryani Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1750 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the chicken breast into large bite-size chunks and marinate in the Greek yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and salt for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear; this keeps the biryani fluffy instead of gummy.
Melt the butter in your largest heavy pot over medium heat and cook the sliced onions 10 to 12 minutes until deep golden. Set a third of them aside for the top.
Add the marinated chicken with all its marinade, plus the cumin, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaves. Cook 5 to 6 minutes until the chicken firms up.
Add the rinsed rice, sliced jalapeno, most of the mint, salt, and the right amount of water for your rice (about 2 cups water per cup of dry rice, minus the marinade moisture). Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly and simmer on the lowest heat 20 minutes, then rest off the heat, still covered, 10 minutes. No peeking; the steam is doing the work.
Check that the chicken reads 165F, pull the bay leaves, and fluff gently with a fork. Top with the reserved golden onions and remaining mint.

name: Chicken Bulgogi Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4 lb (1811 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, zero-sugar soda, chicken broth, minced garlic, grated ginger, sesame oil, salt and black pepper into a marinade until the sugar dissolves.
Slice the chicken thighs thin, about a quarter inch, and turn them in the marinade until every piece is coated. Refrigerate at least 4 hours and preferably overnight.
Cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes while the oven heats to 450F.

Lift the chicken out of the marinade, letting the excess drip off, and spread it in a single layer across two sheet pans. Crowding it will steam the meat and you will lose the caramelized edges you came for.
Roast 15 to 18 minutes, then run the broiler for 2 to 3 minutes until the edges char and the sugar in the marinade turns dark and sticky. Watch it closely; sugar goes from beautiful to ruined fast.
Pour the leftover marinade into a small pot, bring it to a hard boil for a full 2 minutes, and reduce it into a glaze. Boiling is not optional, since raw chicken sat in it.
Chop the roasted chicken, toss it in the reduced glaze in your mixing pot, and fold the cooked rice through.

name: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3 lb (1307 g)
Cream of Chicken Soup (generic condensed (USDA)): 2.3 cans (695 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350F and cook the rice, since it goes into the dish rather than under it.
Cook the chicken breast and cut it into bite sized pieces.

In a large bowl, stir together the cream of chicken soup, sour cream, dijon mustard, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper into a smooth sauce. The dijon is not optional. It is what keeps a rich casserole from tasting flat.
Fold in the cooked rice, chicken, and diced ham until everything is coated.
Spread half the mixture into a large baking dish, layer the swiss cheese across it, then add the rest of the mixture on top.
Crush the butter crackers, toss them with the melted butter, and scatter them over the surface in an even layer.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until it bubbles around the edges and the topping is golden, then rest 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Chicken Divan (Broccoli Cheese Bake)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 2.25 lb (980 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
Cream of Mushroom Soup (Campbell's (USDA SR)): 2.3 cans (695 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350F. Thaw the broccoli and press it dry in a towel. Do not skip the drying step, because every drop of water you leave in ends up thinning the sauce.
Cook the chicken breast, then cut or shred it into bite sized pieces.
In a large bowl, stir together the cream of mushroom soup, sour cream, milk, most of the shredded cheddar, garlic powder, onion powder, dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
Fold the chicken and broccoli into the sauce until everything is coated evenly.
Spread it into a large baking dish and scatter the rest of the cheddar over the top.
Toss the bread crumbs with the melted butter and sprinkle them over the cheese. This is what gives you a crunchy top instead of a soft one.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until it bubbles at the edges and the crumbs are golden. Cook the rice while it bakes and rest the dish 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 1.75 lb (844 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice a day ahead, spread it on a sheet pan, and chill it uncovered in the fridge overnight. This is not optional if you want real fried rice.
Dice the chicken breast small and toss it with a spoonful of cornstarch, a splash of soy sauce, and the chicken broth. Let it sit 15 minutes so it stays tender in a screaming hot pan.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat a little of the vegetable oil in your largest skillet, scramble them just until set, and slide them out onto a plate.
Add more oil, get the pan very hot, and cook the chicken in a single layer until browned and cooked through. Remove it.

Add the rest of the oil and the diced onion and cook 2 minutes, then add the cold rice and press it into the pan. Let it sit undisturbed for a minute at a time so it toasts instead of steaming. Constant stirring is the most common fried rice mistake.
Return the chicken and eggs, add the remaining soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, salt, and pepper, and toss everything together for two minutes.
Kill the heat and fold in the sliced green onions.

name: Chicken Jalfrezi
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.75 lb (2100 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dried chiles in hot water for 15 minutes and blend them smooth with a little of the soaking liquid.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite sized pieces and toss with turmeric, salt, and a spoonful of the white vinegar.
Start the rice.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet and sear the chicken hard until browned at the edges, then pull it out. It does not need to be cooked through yet.
Cook the sliced onions until golden, add the garlic and the blended chile paste, then the cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, garam masala, and chili powder and toast them for a minute.

Add the tomato paste and the canned tomatoes and simmer hard, uncovered, until the sauce thickens and darkens and the oil starts to separate, about 20 minutes. This reduction is the whole difference between jalfrezi and a watery tomato curry.
Return the chicken with the bell peppers and cook 6 to 8 minutes, just until the chicken is done and the peppers are still crisp. Finish with the rest of the vinegar and a big handful of cilantro.

name: Chicken Kabsa (Saudi Spiced Chicken and Rice)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1588 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear and let it drain. This is what keeps kabsa fluffy instead of sticky.
Heat the olive oil in a wide heavy pot and brown the chicken thighs on both sides, then set them aside.
Cook the chopped onion until soft, then add the garlic and ginger for a minute.

Stir in the tomato paste and all the spices, cinnamon, cumin, coriander, garam masala, nutmeg, cloves, paprika, salt, and pepper, and toast them in the oil for 30 seconds until the pot smells like a spice market.
Add the diced tomatoes and grated carrots, return the chicken, add water to cover, and simmer covered for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Pull the chicken out and set it aside.

Add the drained rice to the pot, make sure the liquid sits about an inch above it, bring it to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes. Do not lift the lid, because every peek costs you steam.
Rest it covered off the heat for 10 minutes, then rest the chicken back on top, add the lime juice, and fold in the toasted almonds and golden raisins.

name: Chicken Katsu Curry Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Start the rice: rinse 4.25 cups dry rice and cook it in your rice cooker or a covered pot while everything else happens.

Make the curry base: heat the vegetable oil in your big pot and cook the sliced onions over medium heat 15 to 20 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic, curry powder, and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.

Add the chopped potatoes, carrots, chicken broth, Worcestershire sauce, and sugar. Simmer 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender, then stir in the cornstarch mixed with a little cold water and the butter. Simmer until the sauce thickens and coats a spoon. Season with salt and pepper.
Bread the chicken: slice the breasts into cutlets about a half inch thick. Dredge each in flour, then beaten egg, then bread crumbs, pressing the crumbs on.
Fry the cutlets in batches in a skillet with a thin layer of oil, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and the inside reads 165 F on a thermometer. Rest on a rack, then slice into strips.
Portion rice into 14 containers, ladle curry sauce over, and top with sliced katsu. Keeping the katsu on top helps it stay crisper in the fridge.

name: Chicken Lo Mein Noodle Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 31.5 oz dry (892 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 4.5 oz (126 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the sauce: hoisin, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, chicken broth, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth. Set it by the stove.
Boil the egg noodles 1 minute short of the package time, drain, and toss with a little oil so they do not clump.
Slice the chicken breast into thin strips. Working in batches, sear in vegetable oil over high heat until cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
In the same pot, stir fry the sliced red bell pepper 2 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, and most of the green onions for 1 minute more.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce, and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens and turns glossy.
Add the noodles and toss until every strand is coated. Finish with the remaining green onions.
Portion into 14 containers while still warm so the sauce distributes evenly.

name: Chicken Madras Curry
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1750 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken into chunks and marinate it with the lemon juice, chili powder, salt and half the minced garlic for at least 30 minutes while you prep everything else.
Melt the butter in your largest pot over medium and cook the diced onion for 8 minutes until soft and browning at the edges, then add the rest of the garlic and the grated ginger and cook one minute.
Add the curry powder and garam masala and stir them in the hot butter for 45 seconds until they bloom and stop smelling raw.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook down for 8 to 10 minutes, until the sauce darkens and thickens and the fat starts to come to the surface.
Stir in the marinated chicken along with the sliced carrots and diced red bell pepper. Cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the chicken reads 165F and the carrots are tender.
Stir in the coconut milk, the sugar, the lime juice and the black pepper, and let it come back to a bare simmer for 5 minutes. Taste it: madras should be hot first and sour second.
Cook the rice, let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes, then fold it through the curry with the chopped cilantro.

name: Chicken Maqluba (Palestinian Upside-Down Rice)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1746 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and leave it to soak while you cook everything else.

Cube the eggplant, toss it with some of the olive oil and salt, and roast it at 425F for 20 to 25 minutes with the broccoli florets on a second pan until both are browned at the edges. Roasting instead of frying saves you a lot of oil.

Meanwhile, brown the chicken thighs in the rest of the olive oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high, seasoned with the ground allspice, ground cinnamon, garam masala, ground turmeric, salt and black pepper.
Add the diced onion and garlic to the pot for 4 minutes, then the diced tomatoes and bay leaves. Cook 5 minutes until the tomato darkens.
Layer it properly: chicken and sauce on the bottom of the pot, then the roasted eggplant and broccoli, then the drained rice spread evenly across the top. Do not stir it. The layers are the recipe.

Pour hot water or broth gently over the back of a spoon until the liquid sits about an inch above the rice. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat 30 to 35 minutes, then rest it covered another 15 minutes off the heat.
Scoop it out in sections rather than flipping it, toasting the almonds in a dry pan while you work, and scatter them over the top.

name: Chicken Marbella
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 5 lb (2217 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Make the marinade by combining the red wine vinegar, olive oil, garlic, oregano, bay leaves, olives, capers with a little of their brine, golden raisins, salt, and pepper.
Cut the chicken breast into large pieces, put them in the marinade, and refrigerate overnight. Marbella genuinely does not work with a thirty minute marinade, so plan this one a day ahead.
Heat the oven to 350F. Spread the chicken and all the marinade into a large baking dish in a single layer so everything roasts rather than steams.
Sprinkle the brown sugar over the top and pour the chicken broth around the edges, not over the sugar.
Roast 45 to 50 minutes, basting with the pan juices two or three times along the way. The basting is what builds the glaze, so it is worth opening the oven for.
Cook the rice while the chicken roasts.
Let the pan rest 10 minutes, then pull the bay leaves and slice the chicken. The juices in the bottom of the pan are the sauce, so do not leave any of them behind.

name: Chicken Mole Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Char the poblanos under the broiler or over a burner flame until blistered all over. Steam them in a covered bowl 10 minutes, then peel, seed, and roughly chop.
Cook the rice: 4.75 cups dry rice in your rice cooker or a covered pot while the sauce comes together.
In your big pot, saute the chopped onion and jalapeno until soft. Add the chili powder, garlic powder, oregano, and black pepper and toast 1 minute.
Blend the poblanos, onion mixture, peanuts, and about half the chicken broth until smooth. Pour the sauce back into the pot with the rest of the broth.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks, season with salt, and simmer them in the sauce 20 to 25 minutes until they reach 165 F and the sauce has thickened.
Portion rice into 14 containers, ladle chicken and mole sauce over, and finish with chopped cilantro.

name: Chicken Normandy (Apple Cider Braised Chicken)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.25 lb (1470 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and thyme and brown them in the olive oil and butter until they have real color on both sides. Set them aside.
Cook the sliced onions in the same pan until soft and golden, then add the garlic for a minute.
Add the apples cut into thick wedges and cook 3 or 4 minutes just until they start to color at the edges. Do not cook them soft yet, because they still have the braise to get through.
Pour in the apple juice and chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pan clean, then return the chicken.
Cover and simmer 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the liquid has reduced by about a third.
Stir the dijon mustard into the heavy cream in a bowl first, then add that mixture to the pan off the boil. Cream added to a hard boiling pan can split, and the mustard tempers it.
Simmer gently 5 more minutes until the sauce coats a spoon. Cook the rice and taste the sauce for salt before portioning.

name: Chicken Pad Thai Noodle Bowls
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 30.75 oz dry (875 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 6.75 oz (189 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 2.25 lb (1050 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the rice noodles in hot tap water 20 to 30 minutes until pliable but not fully soft, then drain. They finish cooking in the pot.
Stir the sauce together: fish sauce, brown sugar, oyster sauce, and lime juice. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Slice the chicken thin, season with salt and pepper, and sear it in batches in a little of the oil over high heat until cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the sliced onion and garlic in more oil until fragrant. Push everything to one side, pour in the beaten eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss and fry 2 to 3 minutes, until the noodles soak up the sauce and turn glossy. Return the chicken and toss once more.
Portion into 14 containers and top each with a spoonful of chopped peanuts so they keep their crunch.

name: Chicken Pot Pie Casserole with Biscuits
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 1.75 lb (794 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 375F. Dice the potatoes small and boil them until just tender, then drain. Small dice matters, because big chunks will still be hard when the biscuits are done.
Cook the diced chicken breast in a little of the butter until browned and cooked through, then set it aside.
Melt the rest of the butter in a large pot, cook the diced onion until soft, add the garlic, then whisk in the flour and cook it for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken broth and milk slowly while whisking, then simmer until it thickens into a proper gravy. Season with the poultry seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Fold in the chicken, potatoes, and frozen peas and pour everything into a large baking dish.
Separate the biscuits and arrange them across the top with a little space between each one so they can spread and brown.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the biscuits are deep golden on top and cooked through underneath. Pale biscuits mean raw dough in the middle, so trust the color and not the timer.

name: Chicken Provencal
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and italian seasoning and brown them in the olive oil in batches. Set them aside.
Cook the sliced onions in the same pan until soft and lightly browned, then add the garlic for a minute.
Add the cherry tomatoes whole and cook over medium-high heat until they blister and start to burst, about 6 minutes. Press a few with the back of a spoon to get things moving.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pan, then return the chicken with any juices.
Simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced enough to cling instead of run.
Add the olives and capers in the last 5 minutes. Adding them early makes the whole pot too salty, and once that happens there is no way back.
Cook the rice, then taste the sauce and adjust the salt, keeping in mind the olives brought their own.

name: Chicken Rogan Josh
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.75 lb (3500 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dried chiles in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend them with a little of the soaking liquid into a smooth red paste. That paste is the color and the soul of the dish.
Whisk the greek yogurt with the milk until it is completely smooth and pourable. Cold, thick yogurt is what splits, so take the minute.
Heat the vegetable oil and butter together in your largest heavy pot over medium-high, add the bay leaves, and let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Add the chicken thighs and sear them, working in batches so the pot stays hot. Return them all to the pot with the minced garlic and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the chile paste, chili powder, ground fennel, ground ginger, ground coriander, ground cumin and salt and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the oil turns red and separates.

Turn the heat to low and add the yogurt mixture a ladle at a time, stirring constantly and letting each addition come together before the next goes in. Rushing this is how you end up with curdled sauce.
Cover and simmer gently 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is glossy, then stir in the garam masala off the heat.

name: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 4.75 lb (2183 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken breast into large pieces, season it with the cajun seasoning, and brown it in the vegetable oil in a heavy pot. Set it aside.

Melt the butter in the same pot, whisk in the flour, and now settle in. Stir constantly over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes until the roux turns the color of milk chocolate. Do not answer the phone. If black flecks appear, throw it out and start over, because a burnt roux poisons the entire pot.
Add the diced onion, bell pepper, and celery straight into the hot roux. It will hiss and stop the cooking, which is exactly what you want. Cook 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, thyme, smoked paprika, italian seasoning, bay leaves, salt, and pepper and stir for a minute.
Pour in the chicken broth slowly while whisking so the roux incorporates smoothly instead of clumping, then return the chicken.
Simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, skimming any fat that rises. The gumbo should thicken to the point where it coats a spoon but still pours.
Cook the rice, then stir the sliced green onions in off the heat.

name: Chicken Scampi
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6 lb (2778 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (1 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti 1 minute short of package time, drain, and toss with a spoonful of oil so it does not clump.
Slice the chicken into strips, season with salt and pepper, and dredge in the flour. Sear in batches in vegetable oil until golden and cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
In the same pot, saute the sliced green and red bell peppers with the red and yellow onion until they soften with a little char, about 5 minutes. Set aside with the chicken.
Melt the butter, add the garlic and red pepper flakes, and cook 1 minute. Sprinkle in a couple spoonfuls of the leftover dredging flour and whisk 1 minute more.
Whisk in the chicken broth and lemon juice and simmer until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon. Stir in the parsley.
Return the chicken, peppers, and onions, then toss with the spaghetti and half the parmesan.
Portion into 14 containers and top with the remaining parmesan.

name: Chicken Souvlaki Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 4 lb (1826 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Marinate the chicken: cube the breasts and toss with most of the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Let it sit at least 30 minutes in the fridge.
Cook the rice: 4.5 cups dry rice in a rice cooker or covered pot.
Roast the vegetables: toss the chopped zucchini, red onion, and bell pepper with the remaining oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 425 F for 20 to 25 minutes until browned at the edges.
Sear the marinated chicken in a hot skillet in batches, 6 to 8 minutes, until charred at the edges and cooked through to 165 F.
Make the yogurt sauce: stir the Greek yogurt with the grated cucumber (squeeze the water out first), a spoon of garlic, a squeeze of lemon juice, and a pinch of salt.
Portion rice into 14 containers, then divide the chicken, roasted vegetables, olives, and halved cherry tomatoes. Pack the yogurt sauce in small cups on the side so it stays cold and fresh.

name: Chicken Tetrazzini
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 2 lb (871 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 9.25 oz (264 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 375F. Boil the spaghetti two minutes short of the package time and drain it. It will finish cooking in the oven, and fully cooked pasta going into a bake comes out mushy.
Cook the chicken breast in the olive oil, then cut or shred it into bite sized pieces.

Brown the sliced mushrooms in a dry hot pan first, without crowding, until they release their water and it cooks off. Adding fat too early makes them steam, and steamed mushrooms make a watery casserole.
Add the butter, onion, and garlic to the mushrooms and cook until soft, then sprinkle in the flour and cook it for 2 minutes.
Whisk in the chicken broth slowly, then the heavy cream, and simmer until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon. Finish it with the lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Fold in the spaghetti and chicken, then spread everything into a large baking dish and scatter the mozzarella over the top.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling and browned on top, then rest 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Chicken Vesuvio
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.5 lb (3360 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the potatoes into thick wedges and toss them with some of the olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Season the chicken thighs with salt, pepper, oregano, and italian seasoning, then brown them hard in the rest of the olive oil in a large oven safe pan. Set them aside.
Add the potato wedges to the same pan cut side down and let them take on color for 5 minutes without moving them. That crust is the whole point of vesuvio potatoes.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, then pour in the chicken broth and lemon juice and scrape the bottom of the pan.
Nestle the chicken back in among the potatoes, put the pan in the oven, and roast 30 to 35 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir the butter into the pan juices off the heat so the sauce goes glossy.
Scatter the frozen peas over the top and let the residual heat warm them through, about 3 minutes. Do not roast them or they turn gray and sad.

name: Chicken Vindaloo
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.75 lb (3500 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dried chiles in hot water for 20 minutes until they soften, then drain and reserve some of the soaking liquid.

Blend the soaked chiles with the garlic, ginger, white vinegar, lime juice, dijon mustard, coriander, cumin, cinnamon, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and sugar into a smooth paste. Add soaking liquid until the blender moves. Taste it and brace yourself, because it is meant to be intense at this stage.
Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces and toss them with about a third of the paste. Let them sit at least an hour in the fridge.

Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and cook the sliced onions slowly until they go deep golden brown, about 20 minutes. This is where the sweetness that balances the vinegar comes from, so do not stop at pale yellow.
Add the rest of the paste and fry it in the oil for 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and the oil separates out at the edges.
Add the chicken with its marinade and the tomato sauce, bring it to a simmer, and cook uncovered 30 to 35 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce clings.
Taste for salt and vinegar. Vindaloo should finish sharp, so add a splash more vinegar if it has gone flat.

name: Slow Cooker Chile Colorado Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stem and seed the guajillo and ancho chiles along with the arbol chiles from the pantry list, and toast them briefly in a dry pan until fragrant.
Soak the toasted chiles in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend them with the onion, garlic, oregano, cumin, and a cup of the soaking liquid until smooth. Strain the sauce.
Cut the chuck roast into large cubes, season with salt and black pepper, and toss them in the flour.
Brown the floured beef in the olive oil in batches in a heavy pot, working in batches so the flour crisps rather than steams.
Return all the beef, pour in the strained chile sauce and the beef broth, and add the bay leaves.
Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 2 to 2.5 hours, stirring now and then, until the beef is fork tender and the sauce has darkened and thickened.
Pull the bay leaves, taste for salt, and cook the rice separately.

name: Chile Relleno Casserole with Ground Beef
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Broil the poblano peppers on a sheet pan, turning once, until the skins blister and blacken, then steam them in a covered bowl for ten minutes and slip the skins off.
Slit the peppers open, pull out the seeds, and lay them flat.
Brown the ground beef with the diced yellow onion, salt, and black pepper until no pink remains, then drain the fat.
Layer half the poblanos in a large greased baking dish, spread the beef over them, scatter on most of the cheddar cheese, and top with the remaining poblanos.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, all-purpose flour, a dash of hot sauce, and salt until smooth with no lumps.
Pour the custard evenly over the layers and let it settle for a few minutes so it works its way down.
Bake at 350 degrees until the center is set and no longer jiggles, scatter the last of the cheddar on top, and bake a few minutes more until melted. Cook the rice separately to serve underneath.

name: Chili Cornbread Casserole
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 1.8 cans (757 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground beef in olive oil in your big pot, breaking it up until no pink remains. Add the diced onion and green bell pepper and cook until soft.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cayenne, brown sugar, and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until dark and fragrant.
Add the Worcestershire, hot sauce, chicken broth, crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, and drained kidney beans. Simmer uncovered 20 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the chili into a greased baking dish (or two, this is a big batch). Heat the oven to 375 F.
Mix the cornbread topping: corn muffin mix, drained corn, milk, sour cream, melted butter, and eggs. Stir just until combined and spread it gently over the chili.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until the cornbread is golden and a toothpick in the topping comes out clean.
Cool 15 minutes, then portion into 14 containers, making sure each gets its share of the cornbread lid.

name: Chipotle Sweet Potato Pork Chili
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 1.5 cans (393 g)
Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 5 tbsp (83 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cube the pork shoulder, pat it dry, season with salt, black pepper, chili powder, smoked paprika, ground cumin and a pinch of ground allspice, and brown it hard in the olive oil in batches.
Cook the diced onion and chopped poblano peppers in the same pot until soft, then add the minced garlic and the chopped chipotles in adobo and stir for a minute.
Stir in the Dijon mustard, the red wine vinegar and the splash of fish sauce, which sounds strange and is the reason this chili tastes like it cooked twice as long.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice, return the pork, and simmer covered for about 2 hours until the pork shreds.
Add the cubed sweet potatoes and both drained beans and simmer another 30 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender and starting to break apart and thicken the pot.
Warm the tortillas and keep the sour cream and chopped cilantro in separate containers for topping at reheat.

name: Chorizo & Potato Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the potatoes into half-inch cubes, toss with olive oil, salt, chili powder, and garlic powder, and roast at 425 F for 30 to 35 minutes until crispy, flipping once.

While the potatoes roast, brown the chorizo in your big pot over medium heat, breaking it up, 8 to 10 minutes until fully cooked and starting to crisp. Pork chorizo is done when it reads 160 F or higher and no pink remains.
Add the diced red bell pepper to the chorizo and cook 4 to 5 minutes until softened in the rendered fat.
Make the quick salsa: finely chop the tomatillos and stir with the cilantro, lime juice, and a pinch of salt and black pepper. For a smoother salsa, pulse it in a blender.
Fold the roasted potatoes into the chorizo and peppers so everything gets coated.
Portion into 14 containers and spoon the tomatillo salsa over each, or pack it on the side to keep it bright.

name: Chuletas Guisadas Stewed Pork Chops and Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the pork chops all over with sazon, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper, and let them sit while you prep.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot and sear the chops in batches until browned on both sides, then set them aside.
Add the diced yellow onion and green bell peppers to the pot and cook until soft, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in the garlic, salsa, and white vinegar and cook for a minute.
Add the tomato sauce, chicken broth, olives, and bay leaves, then return the chops and any juices to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the pork is tender enough to pull apart with a fork, then uncover and let the gravy thicken.
Cook the rice according to the package, fish out the bay leaves, and finish the stew with the chopped cilantro.

name: Classic Beef Stew with Potatoes and Carrots
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into large cubes, pat them completely dry, and season with salt and black pepper.
Brown the beef in the olive oil in batches over high heat, giving each piece room. This is the step that makes the stew, so take your time.
Cook the chopped onion, garlic, carrots, and celery in the same pot until they soften and pick up the browned bits.
Stir in the flour and the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes so the flour loses its raw taste.
Return the beef and pour in the beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Add the bay leaves and thyme.
Cover and simmer very low for 2 to 2.5 hours, until the beef is tender enough to break with a spoon.
Add the cubed potatoes for the last 30 minutes, then pull the bay leaves and correct the salt and pepper.

name: Claypot Chicken and Mushroom Rice
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1588 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 0.5 cups (126 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite sized pieces and marinate them with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil, and a little salt and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms and the sausage thin. Thin matters, because everything on top needs to cook through in the same time the rice does.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then put it in a heavy pot or rice cooker with the chicken broth.
Lay the marinated chicken, mushrooms, and sausage across the top of the rice. Do not stir. The rice steams underneath while the toppings drip down into it, and stirring destroys the whole method.
Cook covered on low for about 25 minutes, or run a standard rice cooker cycle, then let it sit covered off the heat for 10 more minutes.
Lift the lid, pour any remaining marinade over the top, and now fold everything together gently.
Scatter the sliced green onions across the pot before portioning.

name: Cochinita Pibil Pork Rice Bowls
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 1.25 tbsp (18 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the achiote paste with the orange juice, apple cider vinegar, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and black pepper until it is a smooth brick red marinade.
Cut the pork shoulder into large chunks, coat every piece in the marinade, and let it sit at least an hour or overnight in the fridge.
Put the pork and all the marinade in the slow cooker with the beef broth and cook on low for 8 hours, until it falls apart under a fork.
Slice the red onion paper thin, cover it in the lime juice with a pinch of salt, and let it sit at room temperature until it turns pink.
Shred the pork right in the cooking liquid so it soaks the sauce back up. Do not drain it, that red liquid is the whole point.
Cook the rice per the package and warm the tortillas just before you assemble.

name: Colombian Pork Loin with Blackberry Sauce
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 375F. Pat the pork loin dry and rub it all over with minced garlic, salt and black pepper.
Sear the loin in a hot pan on every side until it takes on color, then move it to a roasting pan.
Roast until the center reaches 145F, then pull it out and let it rest at least ten minutes before you touch it. Cutting early dumps all the juice on the board.
While the pork roasts, put the blackberries, sugar, lime juice and chicken broth in a saucepan and simmer until the berries collapse.
Press the sauce through a strainer to catch the seeds, then return it to the pan and reduce until it coats a spoon.
Cook the rice per the package so it is hot when everything else is ready.
Slice the rested pork thin against the grain, then combine the rice, sliced pork and blackberry sauce in your big pot.

name: Coq au Vin
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.25 lb (126 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the chopped bacon in a heavy pot until crisp, then lift it out and leave the fat behind.
Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper and brown them hard in the bacon fat in batches. This is the color of the finished dish, so take it further than feels comfortable.
Add the quartered onions and carrots and cook until they take on color, then add the garlic and tomato paste and cook another minute.
Pour in the beef broth and chicken broth, scraping every brown bit off the bottom, and add the thyme and bay leaves. Return the chicken and the bacon.
Cover and simmer low for about 45 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the vegetables are soft.
Brown the mushrooms separately in butter over high heat and add them at the end. Mushrooms thrown in at the start turn gray and rubbery, and browning them apart is what keeps them worth eating.
Knead the rest of the butter with flour into a paste and stir it into the simmering pot a little at a time until the sauce coats a spoon. Cook the rice and serve the braise over it.
